newsitem.title: THAILAND: National Finance to lose if baht dips under 28.51.
newsitem.headline: National Finance to lose if baht dips under 28.51.

text.p: Thai broker National Finance and Securities Plc said on Thursday it will be exposed to foreign exchange losses if the baht fall below 28.51 to the dollar.
The Bank of Thailand on Thursday set a baht/dollar reference rate of 27.383 which reflects average trade by commercial banks on Wednesday.
The government dropped its system of pegging the baht to a basket of currencies on Wednesday and floated the baht.
The baht dropped about 15-20 percent on Wednesday and was trading around 29.20/29.40 to the dollar offshore and 27.500 onshore early on Thursday.
National Finance firm said it has $450 million dollars in foreign denominated liabilities of which $386 is fully protected from exchange fluctuations.
The balance of $64.50 million is only partly protected by reserves for possible foreign exchange losses, the firm said.

National Finance said its total reserves are 167 million baht ($5.95 million) and would protect the firm from accounting losses up to a spot rate of 25.81 baht per dollar.($1 = 28 baht) -- Bangkok newsroom (662) 652-0642
